products.name: InternLM (Shanghai AI Lab)
products.note: Chinese open-source LLM; academic research; cross-border data review advised

reading.body:
Shanghai AI Laboratory is a government-affiliated research institution in China operating InternLM, an open-source large language model positioned for academic research across Chinese universities and scientific applications.

The laboratory's stated focus spans model capability, embodied robotics, and AI safety frameworks, with recent emphasis on science-oriented systems that integrate language models, specialist agents, and physical automation. This portfolio suggests a research strategy prioritizing broad capability development rather than any single domain constraint. The 2026 announcement of AI-for-science results and a scientific discovery platform indicates the institution is testing large models as infrastructure for experimental workflows, from hypothesis through validation.

What matters for AI infrastructure is that Shanghai AI Laboratory operates within China's university and research ecosystem, not as a commercial infrastructure builder or power provider. The laboratory contributes to model capability and research methodology but does not control the compute, buildings, or power grids that determine how quickly those capabilities can scale. It represents the downstream user of infrastructure, not the constraint that binds it.

The data does not cover the laboratory's budget, its access to compute hardware, or the power requirements of its training and inference systems. Without those facts, the connection between its research ambitions and the infrastructure constraints that may or may not enable them remains unmeasured.

profile_text.body:
Shanghai AI Laboratory is a non-profit government laboratory, according to its own site, working toward AGI. The site describes recruiting young researchers worldwide in areas including artificial intelligence, large models, embodied intelligence, trustworthy AI, AI for Science, basic platforms, the innovation chain and management support, and advertises a "North Star" talent plan. Since 2022 it has run a joint doctoral training program with more than ten universities, among them Peking University, Tsinghua University, Fudan University, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Tongji University, the University of Science and Technology of China and Zhejiang University.

The laboratory's tracked product is InternLM, listed as a Chinese open-source LLM used in academic research, with cross-border data review advised. Its site describes a general-specialty integration technical system in three layers: a foundation model layer, a fusion and coordination layer, and an exploration and evolution layer. It also describes the 书生·端砚 science discovery platform, upgraded and fully opened as a full-stack service at the 2026 Pujiang Innovation Forum; the 书生 physical world model W0; the 书生 science multimodal large model S2; and Intern-Robotics, an embodied full-stack engine. At the 2026 WAIC science frontier forum it says it released ten joint innovation results with universities, research institutes and industry partners, covering life sciences, materials science and deep space astronomy.

On safety, the site describes an "AI-45 degree balance law" and a causal path toward trustworthy AGI through three stages, 泛对齐, 可干预 and 能反思, supported by a digital twin platform, an intelligent verification matrix and a data evolution flywheel. Professor 周伯文 is quoted proposing that scientific research is the next programming and that AI and science will form a two-wheel drive. The site also describes a capability combining vision, force and touch sensing for real experiments, including gene editing protein directed evolution, 美哌卡因 organic synthesis and lipid nanoparticle synthesis.
